items.q: Can reps use Trackeys with no internet signal?
items.a: Yes. The mobile app is offline-first: visits, orders, invoices and payments all work without connectivity. Data syncs automatically when signal returns, with conflict-free merge for any edits made on the server while the device was offline.

items.q: How does the AI copilot make suggestions?
items.a: The copilot runs on aggregated visit history, order patterns and customer attributes. It suggests next-best-actions (upsell, cross-sell, re-engagement) and flags churn risk, always with a short explanation so the rep understands the reasoning.

items.q: Does it support multiple currencies, taxes and languages?
items.a: Yes. Multi-currency pricing, multi-tax jurisdictions (VAT, GST), and localized UI for English, Arabic, French and other regional languages are built in.

items.q: How are pricing and discount rules enforced?
items.a: Pricing rules, approval limits and discount tiers are configured per role and per customer segment. Reps can only quote within their authority; anything above routes to an approval workflow with a full audit trail.

items.q: What routing algorithms does Trackeys use?

items.q: How accurate is live tracking?

items.q: Does it handle cold chain / temperature monitoring?

items.q: How accurate is the vision AI?
items.a: SKU recognition accuracy averages 99%+ for well-lit shelf photos of products in the trained catalog. New SKUs can be added via few-shot learning, typically 10–20 reference images per SKU get the model to production accuracy.

items.q: Does it work in low light or on messy shelves?
items.a: Yes, the model is trained on a large dataset of real-world retail photos including poor lighting, partial occlusion and disordered shelves. For extreme conditions the app prompts the merchandiser to reshoot with guidance.

items.q: Can I define custom planograms?
items.a: Absolutely. Planograms are uploaded per store + category, with flexibility for retailer-specific layouts. The AI scores against whichever planogram applies at that specific store on that specific visit.

items.q: What about competitor data collection?
items.a: Merchandisers can capture competitor prices, facings and promos in the same flow. The data flows into competitive dashboards, useful for pricing teams and brand managers.

items.q: How does per-module pricing work?
items.a: Each tier bundles a set of modules (SFA, Delivery & Routing, Merchandising AI, DMS). If you only need SFA + Delivery, pick Starter. If you need all four, pick Growth. Enterprise unlocks everything plus custom modules and workflows. You can also add Fleet Management as a separate add-on on any tier.

items.q: What counts as a "visit" or a "shelf scan"?
items.a: A visit is a single rep check-in at a store or customer location. A shelf scan is one photo processed by the vision AI (a single aisle typically takes 2–4 scans). Both limits are monthly and reset on your billing anniversary.

items.q: Can we change tiers or add modules mid-contract?
items.a: Yes. You can upgrade at any time and we'll prorate the difference. Downgrades apply at renewal. Adding an add-on (Fleet, Premium Support, etc.) is instant with pro-rated billing to your anniversary.

items.q: Do you offer a free trial?
items.a: Yes, 14 days on Starter or Growth, no credit card required. You get full access to the modules in that tier and we'll help you import sample data so you can evaluate with your own customers and stores.

items.q: What's included in onboarding?
items.a: Starter is self-serve with guided setup videos. Growth includes a 2-week guided onboarding with a specialist (data migration, user training, integration setup). Enterprise gets a white-glove program: 6–12 weeks with a dedicated success manager, custom workflow design and change-management support.

items.q: Is there a discount for nonprofits or education?
items.a: Yes, 40% off Growth for registered nonprofits and 25% off for accredited education institutions. Contact us with documentation to apply.

items.q: How is data security handled?
items.a: SOC 2 Type II certified. AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit. Enterprise plans include SSO, SCIM provisioning, advanced audit logs, data residency options (US, EU, UAE) and optional on-prem deployment.

items.q: What happens if we exceed visit or scan limits?
items.a: You're never blocked. Overages are billed at $0.05 per extra visit and $0.08 per extra shelf scan. We alert you when you hit 80% of your limit so you can upgrade or manage usage proactively.

secondary-sales-visibility.title: Why secondary sales visibility is the FMCG blind spot costing you 20% of revenue.
secondary-sales-visibility.sub: Primary sales leave your warehouse, and visibility drops off a cliff. Here's how modern distributors are closing the gap from plant to shelf, and what it unlocks.
secondary-sales-visibility.author: Imran Shaikh
body: For most FMCG brands, the moment a truck leaves the warehouse is the moment visibility dies. Primary sales are clean, tracked and auditable. Secondary sales (what the distributor actually sells to retail) is a monthly data dump at best, a guess at worst.

We recently audited the distribution data of six mid-market FMCG brands across South Asia and the Gulf. On average, they could answer "what did we ship?" within 2 hours, but "what did our distributors sell?" took 3 weeks. Three weeks of blind spots is three weeks of stock rotting, three weeks of promotions going unreconciled, three weeks of competitors moving faster.
The 20% you're leaving on the table

When you don't see secondary sales in real time, four things go wrong: (1) trade spend gets misallocated against the wrong SKUs, (2) replenishment lags demand and you OOS in fast-moving stores, (3) slow movers hide inside aggregate distributor reports, (4) channel P&L becomes a story instead of a number. Together these account for roughly 15–25% of addressable revenue in most of the brands we've analyzed.
The moment we got secondary-sales visibility down to a day, our promo ROI calculation stopped being theoretical. It became something we acted on, weekly.
What closing the gap looks like

Distributors log secondary sales through a portal or mobile app. Van sales direct to trade is captured at source. Both feed one secondary-sales view with SKU-level traceability. Forecast engines then recalibrate against the new signal, which lifts fill rate, cuts obsolescence, and makes trade spend a knob you can actually turn.

It isn't a tech problem anymore. It's a process problem. Most of the distributors we work with had never been asked for daily data. Once asked, and given a tool that made it 30 seconds of work, they provided it happily.

vision-ai-planogram.title: Vision AI for planograms: from nice-to-have to non-negotiable in 24 months.
vision-ai-planogram.sub: Two years ago, AI shelf audits were a premium upsell. Today, they're table stakes. Here's why, and what makes a good vision model for retail execution.
vision-ai-planogram.author: Fatima Al-Hashimi
body: Three years ago, "AI merchandising" on an RFP meant a shelf-image-capture feature a human auditor would later review. Today, the bar is a real-time detection model that scores planogram compliance, share-of-shelf and out-of-stock on the rep's phone in under 3 seconds.

Two things: model quality got dramatically better for long-tail SKU detection, and phones got fast enough to run inference on-device. The result is that a rep walking into a 200-SKU aisle can get instant, objective compliance scoring: no more human audit queues, no more week-long feedback loops.

SKU-level recall above 94%. Sub-second inference on mid-tier Android devices. Handles edge cases (shelf occlusion, odd lighting, skewed angles) without collapsing confidence. And trained on your actual SKU catalog, not a generic CPG dataset.
Compliance went from a monthly audit we argued about to a daily number the ops team actually managed.

merch-compliance-gap.title: The 30% gap between planned merchandising and what's actually on shelves.
merch-compliance-gap.sub: Why store-level execution so often betrays brand-level strategy, and how to close the gap with measurement that doesn't rely on self-reporting.
merch-compliance-gap.author: Karthik Venkatesh
body: Almost every FMCG brand we benchmark has the same problem: what the trade marketing team plans and what the rep actually executes in-store diverge by an average of 30%. Sometimes more.

Planograms land in a rep's inbox as a PDF. The rep does their best. The auditor, weeks later, scores compliance from memory. Nobody is lying; the feedback loop is just too slow and fuzzy for anyone to act on.

Photo-based compliance scoring with the planogram visible on-screen. Real-time feedback to the rep. Aggregate dashboards that highlight the exact 3 stores out of 400 where compliance is slipping. That's enough to flip merchandising from a lagging audit to a leading signal.

ai-demand-forecasting.title: Stop forecasting demand with Excel. A practical guide to AI replenishment for distribution.
ai-demand-forecasting.sub: Classical forecasts assume tomorrow looks like yesterday. AI models handle promotions, seasonality and new-product launches, without hand-tuning 200 parameters.
ai-demand-forecasting.author: Priya Ramesh
body: Demand forecasting in FMCG distribution is still mostly a spreadsheet exercise. That's not because the spreadsheets are wrong; it's because the people running them are genuinely good at what they do. The problem is ceiling: at a certain SKU × store × week granularity, no human can hold enough context to be accurate.

Three places: handling promo uplift as a continuous signal instead of a flag, recognizing seasonality at long tail (not just the top 20 SKUs), and cold-starting new products off taxonomy instead of history. Plus the obvious one: just doing all of it across millions of SKU-store combos.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
body: This policy explains how Trackeys collects, uses, stores and protects personal data, and the rights you have under the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL). By submitting a form on this site you consent to the processing described below.

When you contact us or fill in a form (e.g. Book a Demo, surveys, registrations) we collect the details you provide (such as your name, email, phone number, company, and any message) along with limited technical metadata (IP address, browser user-agent, referring page) used for security and abuse prevention.
2. Why we use it (purpose & lawful basis)

We process this data to respond to your request, schedule and deliver demos, provide support, and operate and secure our services. Our lawful basis is your consent and our legitimate interest in running the business. You can withdraw consent at any time (see Your rights).

We keep personal data only as long as needed for the purpose it was collected. Demo and contact submissions are retained for up to 12 months after the request is closed, after which they are deleted or anonymized automatically.
We do not sell your personal data. We share it only with service providers that help us operate (e.g. hosting, email delivery) under appropriate safeguards, or where required by law.

Under the PDPL you may request access to, correction of, or erasure of your personal data, and you may withdraw consent. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at the address below and we will respond within the period required by law.
For any privacy request or question, email privacy@trackeys.com.
